name: cross_cta_spin
description: Minimal reproduction of the stream-K (47_ampere_gemm_universal_streamk) cross-CTA spin-barrier DEADLOCK on the x86 wrapper. The wrapper runs CTAs SEQUENTIALLY (one CTA to completion before the next), so a CTA that spins on a global flag set by a PEER CTA that has not run yet waits forever. The kernel is the minimal fixup shape: 2 CTAs, 1 thread each. PHASE A (mode=1, grid=1) is a single-CTA control that exercises REDG (atomicAdd partial) + ATOMG.EXCH (flag set) + acquire-load poll + __threadfence on the SEQUENTIAL path and MUST produce out[0]==base+contrib (proves lift/atomics correct). PHASE B (mode=0, grid=2): OWNER=CTA0 spins on a flag PRODUCER=CTA1 sets; under the sequential wrapper CTA0 runs first so the flag is never set -> the kernel's acquire-poll is a real infinite loop -> DEADLOCK. PHASE B runs on a watchdog thread and the deadlock IS the documented current behavior (passes as characterization). With SLIFTER_EXPECT_CONCURRENT_CTA set (the gate a future cross-CTA execution mode is validated against), PHASE B must instead complete with the correct value.
build_note: host pins args via ArgAt{0x208 desc=0, 0x210 out, 0x218 partials, 0x220 flag, 0x228 base f32, 0x22c contrib f32, 0x230 mode i32}. PHASE B intentionally hangs on the default sequential wrapper; the driver uses a 4s watchdog + detaches the orphaned kernel thread so the process still exits.
result_x86: TEST PASSED (PHASE A out[0]==11.75; PHASE B DEADLOCK REPRODUCED on default sequential wrapper)
